summary: Scans one of two global 32-bit arrays looking for the first negative entry. The byte flag at this+0x174 selects the array: non-zero scans dword_7CD2B8..flt_7CD458 (exclusive), zero scans dword_7CD470..flt_7CD610 (exclusive). Returns the index of the first negative entry, or the full element count when no negative entry exists.

local_names.this[372]: selection flag at offset +0x174 choosing which array to scan
local_names.v2: walking pointer over the first array (dword_7CD2B8..flt_7CD458)
local_names.v3: walking pointer over the second array (dword_7CD470..flt_7CD610)
local_names.result: count of entries scanned before the first negative, or total count

operations.description: Reads the flag byte at this+0x174; non-zero selects the dword_7CD2B8..flt_7CD458 array, zero selects the dword_7CD470..flt_7CD610 array
Walks the selected array element by element (dword_7CD2B8..flt_7CD458 for the first branch, dword_7CD470..flt_7CD610 for the second), accumulating the scanned count
Inside the loop, breaks as soon as the current array element is negative, freezing the accumulated count
Returns the scanned count: the index of the first negative entry if the loop broke early, otherwise the full element count of the scanned array

unresolved: The meaning of a negative entry (existing analysis proposes an empty/invalid slot in a collision/contact array, DERIVED only) is not proven by this packet
The object owning the this+0x174 selection flag is unidentified
Both array ranges end at a bound expressed through flt_7CD458 / flt_7CD610; whether those are true array ends or sentinel addresses is not established
